text: This staff report is a matter that Community Council has delegated authority to make a final decision, provided that it is not amended so that it varies with City policy or by-laws. Transportation Services is reporting on the results of the traffic calming poll undertaken on St. Joseph Street, between Queen's Park Crescent East and Bay Street. The poll provided a response rate of less than the 50 percent plus one ballot required by the traffic calming policy in order to confirm that there is a favourable consensus in the community to install speed humps on the subject section of St. Joseph Street. Accordingly, continuing the process to install speed humps on St. Joseph Street, between Queen's Park Crescent East and Bay Street, is not recommended.

The Toronto and East York Community Council: 1. Directed the City Solicitor to prepare a by-law to alter the roadway to install three speed humps on St. Joseph Street, between Queen's Park Crescent East and Bay Street, generally as shown on Drawing No. 421G-2800, dated December 2017, attached to the report (March 22, 2018) from the Acting Director, Transportation Services, Toronto and East York District. 2. Approved the reduction of the speed limit from 40 km/h to 30 km/h on St. Joseph Street, between Queen's Park Crescent East and Bay Street, when speed humps are installed.
